articles.title: Israel demolishes homes of Palestinians blamed for attack on soldiers
articles.summary: Troops hold at least 12 Palestinians near demolished homes as nearly 5,000 remain displaced from Hebron neighbourhoods
articles.body:
Israeli forces have blown up the homes of two Palestinians who killed two Israeli soldiers in Hebron last week. The demolitions came on the eighth day of a military offensive and siege on the southern city in the occupied West Bank.

Troops demolished the homes of brothers Ahmad and Hammouda al-Jaabeh on Friday, after surrounding the buildings since the morning and sealing off the area. The brothers were killed after carrying out an attack on October 23 near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint, at the western entrance to Hebron, killing two Israeli soldiers and wounding three others.

Reporting from Hebron, Al Jazeera’s Mohammed al-Atrash said army engineers spent at least nine hours inside the homes rigging explosives before detonating them.

When residents tried to approach the site afterwards, large numbers of troops backed by drones moved in and detained at least 12 Palestinians, he said. “Some of these Palestinians are still being detained up to this moment and we monitored live on air their abuse at the hands of the Israeli occupation army,” al-Atrash said.

Israeli forces have fully emptied the Ein Deir Bahha neighbourhood of its residents, he said. Some homes “have been turned into military barracks” and command centres. Hundreds of families in the neighbouring al-Jalda area remain trapped in their homes.

The Hebron municipality said on Tuesday that 4,969 Palestinians from 780 families had been displaced by the offensive . Al-Atrash said Israeli forces had arrested at least 120 Palestinians since the operation began and interrogated hundreds more. At least 13 businesses near the checkpoint have been demolished.

He said Israeli officials had threatened to speed up demolitions in Area C, the part of the West Bank under full Israeli control, in line with measures approved by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich after the attack.

On Friday, dozens of displaced residents, including women, children and older people, protested near the closed al-Jalda roundabout. They demanded an end to the siege and the right to return home.

Raed Nairat, an academic and expert on Israeli affairs speaking from Nablus, told Al Jazeera that the operation’s message had been clear “from day one”.

“It is effectively collective punishment, with the aim of breaking the Palestinians’ will and making him pay a price he cannot bear, as a result of an act he may not have been consulted about and may not be content with,” he said.

Nairat said the operation was driven by political rather than security aims. “It is as if you have turned Palestinian society back to 20 or 40 years ago in terms of fragmentation and turned the entire West Bank into a military zone ruled and controlled by the Israeli army,” he said.

Hamas described the forced displacement and demolitions in Hebron as part of a systematic campaign targeting the Palestinian presence and called for urgent international action.

Elsewhere in the occupied West Bank, Israeli forces detained four Palestinians in raids south of Tulkarem. Soldiers and settlers also attacked or drove off olive harvesters in villages near Bethlehem and Nablus.

Israeli military and settler attacks across the West Bank, including occupied East Jerusalem, have intensified since Israel’s war on Gaza began in October 2023.

articles.title: Isro’s GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission successful: Next-generation navigation satellite placed in orbit; NavIC constellation gets a boost
articles.summary: SRIHARIKOTA: India's regional satellite navigation system, NavIC, which was facing a shortage of operational satellites, got a boost with the successful
articles.body: SRIHARIKOTA: India's regional satellite navigation system, NavIC, which was facing a shortage of operational satellites, got a boost with the successful launch of NVS-03 on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday by Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro).GSLV-F18 carrying 2,250kg next-generation navigation satellite -- NVS-03 -- lifted off from the second launch pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) in Sriharikota at 11.51pm on Friday, as scheduled. It was the 20th flight of the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV). Around 18 minutes later, NVS-03 satellite was placed in a geosynchronous transfer orbit (GTO) of 37,023km apogee and 170km perigee."The rocket has successfully and precisely placed the satellite into its intended elliptical orbit. It achieved a 170km perigee and 38,080km apogee. This is the 5th mission from Sriharikota this year. GSLV has carried 34 tonnes of spacecraft to space so far. We achieved this mission with a turnaround time of just 56 days after the GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission in September. With this launch, we have restored NavIC constellation operation as we need a minimum of four satellites to perform positioning, navigation and timing services," said Isro chairman V Narayanan.He said, “The satellite is healthy, and the solar panel has been deployed. Already three pyro walls are operated, and we have lifted. Every system is totally healthy, and we are going to continue the operation and place the satellite in the intended circular orbit.”NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isro's next-generation navigation satellite system, designed to ensure continuity of services under the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS), operationally known as NavIC. The satellite carries an indigenously developed atomic clock along with procured atomic clocks. It also carries the L1 frequency signal in addition to the existing L5 and S-band signals.NavIC is India's independent regional satellite navigation system, designed to provide positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services across the country and an area extending approximately 1,500km beyond the Indian landmass. The additional L1 signal, alongside the existing signals, is expected to improve compatibility with other satellite navigation systems and widen the potential use of NavIC in civilian applications.The NVS-03 mission is part of Isro's plan to deploy five second-generation navigation satellites -- NVS-01 to NVS-05 -- to augment the existing NavIC constellation and improve continuity and reliability of navigation services.The launch assumes significance as NavIC was unable to provide standalone positioning services because of a shortage of operational satellites. In a written reply to the Lok Sabha on July 29, Union minister of state for space Jitendra Singh said the constellation had only three satellites providing positioning, navigation and timing services, against the minimum four required for basic positioning services. While its timing service remains functional, the addition of NVS-03, once commissioned, could help restore standalone positioning capability."Since NavIC is being used in a multi-constellation environment for most of the use cases, there is no vulnerability for the users. The next NavIC satellite, NVS-03, is ready for launch and two more satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, are in an advanced stage of realisation," the minister had said then.The setback to the constellation followed the failure of NVS-02, launched on Jan 29, 2025, to complete its orbit-raising manoeuvres. An Isro review committee found that an electrical signal had failed to reach a pyro valve in the satellite's oxidiser line, preventing the propulsion system from firing and the satellite from reaching its intended orbit. The failure prompted Isro to undertake corrective measures for subsequent missions.The first satellite in the second-generation series, NVS-01, was launched aboard the GSLV-F12 on May 29, 2023. It was also the first satellite in the series to carry an indigenous atomic clock.The Isro chief said five more launches are planned this financial year. “We are moving closer to Gaganyaan G1 uncrewed flight,” he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: Prince William and Kate Middleton may have been made aware of serious allegations against Meghan Markle’s father, Thomas Markle Sr., after a letter detailing the claims was reportedly sent to the joint office shared by the two royal couples at Kensington Palace in 2019.The correspondence was allegedly written by Thomas Markle Sr.’s former wife, Roslyn Loveless, and was passed on by royal protection officers to Prince Harry and Meghan that year. A source also told the Daily Mail’s Richard Eden that it was “unthinkable” that the Royal Household had not been informed.The insider reportedly said Harry and Meghan would not have received the letter in “isolation”, adding that it was the police’s “duty” to make the Palace aware of the claims and that they would have done so.Thomas Markle Sr. has denied any wrongdoing, dismissing the allegations as “sick lies” in an interview with the Daily Mail. William and Kate have not commented publicly or confirmed whether they were aware of the letter.Meghan reportedly sent a final letter to her fatherThe development comes amid reports that Meghan sent a final letter to her father last year while he was recovering in the Philippines following a leg amputation. According to the Sun on Sunday, the Duchess told him that she considered him an abuser and that he would never meet his grandchildren, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five.Meghan became estranged from her father in the run-up to her 2018 wedding to Prince Harry after he was found to have staged paparazzi photographs. Thomas did not attend the ceremony, and King Charles, then the Prince of Wales, accompanied Meghan down the aisle. Her mother, Doria Ragland, was the only member of her family present at the wedding.Thomas Markle Sr. moved to the Philippines in 2025 after suffering a series of strokes. articles.title: Pakistan army ‘cautiously optimistic’ about US-Iran mediation efforts
articles.summary: Pakistan’s military spokesman warns of ‘powerful spoilers and detractors’ who still believe the conflict serves them.
articles.body:
Pakistan’s army is “cautiously optimistic” ⁠about mediation efforts between Iran and the United States as regional countries seek to revive a ceasefire in the eight-month-old war.

Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, spokesman for Pakistan’s military, suggested on Friday that there were positive signs in attempts to de-escalate the conflict. His comments to the Reuters news agency were the first since a high-level delegation visited Tehran this week.

Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan’s chief mediator, has been to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday, alongside Saudi and Turkish officials.

“Why would the Field Marshal be going twice if it is not for some positivity? So yes, of course,” Chaudhry said when asked whether the trips were a positive ⁠sign.

“The word that we would use is always cautiously optimistic,” added Chaudhry, director general of Inter-Services Public Relations.

He also warned that there are parties seeking to obstruct mediation between the US and Iran.

There are still “powerful spoilers and detractors” who believe conflict serves them, he added without naming them.

Speaking in the garrison city of Rawalpindi, where Pakistan’s armed forces are headquartered, Chaudhry declined to say what was discussed in Tehran or whether the US had backed the trip.

His comments on Friday came as Qatari mediators arrived in Tehran in another apparent bid to negotiate a revival of the June ceasefire that collapsed months later.

Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin joined Pakistan’s Munir in ‌Tehran on Monday.

Their two countries signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan on August 7, saying an attack on any signatory will be treated as an attack on all.

The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement has taken on added significance as the Iran war has redrawn regional alliances and raised fears of a broader Middle East conflict.

While the three signatories say the agreement is aimed at collective deterrence and regional security, analysts see its evolution as closely tied to efforts by regional powers to manage the fallout from the Iran-US confrontation.

After Monday’s talks, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said regional security should be ensured by regional countries without foreign intervention.

The wording of the pact does not bar new ⁠members, Chaudhry said on Friday when asked whether Iran could join.

“Anyone who has a shared vision of collective deterrence ⁠and regional peace, why not? Everyone is most welcome,” he said, adding that it was for the political leadership of the three principal parties to decide.

Asked whether more Pakistani troops were being sent to Saudi Arabia under the agreement, Chaudhry said that would depend on the situation and the decision of both countries’ political leadership.

He said Pakistan was committed to defending Saudi ⁠Arabia and the holy sites of Mecca and Medina. “We are not part of the Yemeni conflict, which is an intra-Yemen conflict,” he added.

Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group has been reignited by the Iran ⁠conflict, stoking fears of a wider war.

articles.title: Children's authors to donate to Sally Rooney amid Palestine Action row
articles.summary: Sally Rooney has halted UK sales amid fears it could constitute a "serious criminal offence".
articles.body:
The children's laureates for Wales and Ireland are to give their book royalties to Sally Rooney after she halted UK sales because of her support for Palestine Action.

Nicola Davies and her Irish counterpart Chris Haughton made the decision after she stopped supplying her novels to booksellers in the UK because of fears her work could constitute a "serious criminal offence".

The Normal People author said in 2025 she intended to carry on using her royalties to support the group , despite it being a proscribed a terrorist organisation in the UK .

Davies said: "I don't think I can say I'm standing up for children in Wales without standing up for children in Palestine."

Speaking about the war in Gaza, Wales' children's literature laureate added: "They are children, they are innocent children. Caught up in something absolutely horrible.

She said she's in no way antisemitic but she cannot "stand by and watch this happen."

Davies said she would donate her royalties from The Day War Came to Rooney - the book tells the story of a young girl forced to flee her home after war destroys her town.

The UK government proscribed Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation in 2025, saying it had a "long history" of criminal damage.

It came after the group claimed responsibility for breaking into RAF Brize Norton last year where two military aircrafts were damaged.

Palestine Action has engaged in activities that have predominantly targeted arms companies since the start of the war in Gaza.

There are 84 organisations proscribed under the Terrorism Act 2000 , including al-Qaeda, a jihadist network founded by the late Osama Bin Laden, as well as neo-Nazi group National Action and private Russian military company the Wagner Group.

"It's a ridiculous situation... the British government have dug themselves into a very big hole," said Davies about the Palestine Action ban.

"It's not about politics, belief systems, it's about humanity."

Davies said Gaza was half the size of the Welsh county of Flintshire and compared the war there between Israel and Hamas to Wales having all of its children located there and being bombed.

"The population of Palestine has a very high proportion of children, they have been disproportionally impacted... there are tens of thousands of amputees under the age of 10."

Israel launched its military campaign in Gaza in response to the Hamas-led attack on the country on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, including at least 21,976 children, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

The UN says another 10,000 children in Gaza have sustained life-changing injuries, including permanent disabilities.

Asked if she was concerned about any potential repercussions for donating her royalties to Rooney, Davies said: "Of course - but the repercussions for those in Gaza are horrific."

She said she understood Palestine Action was a proscribed group, but added: "As far as British law is concerned, I'm not doing anything illegal.

"I'm not donating to Palestine Action, I'm donating to Sally Rooney as an act of solidarity."

Rooney has sold more than six million books globally, including 2.3 million in the UK, according to NielsenIQ BookData.

Normal People was published in 2018 and turned into a hit TV series two years later, effectively launching the acting careers of Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones.

Rooney's other novels are Intermezzo, Conversations With Friends and Beautiful World, Where Are You.

Ebook editions of her books have been removed from sale in the UK, although many book shops still have existing stock.

In a previous statement, regarding her decision to stop supplying UK booksellers as a result of her support for Palestine Action, Rooney said: "I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences."

In 2025, Haughton co-wrote a statement in support of ending arms sales to Israel and in support of Palestine Action.

He said he would donate the proceeds from his UK book sales to Rooney and "it's up to her what she does with it".

"As a children's author I cannot work while these atrocities continue," he added, in a statement.

Labour called for a ceasefire for the first time in February 2024 and the UK voted in favour of UN Security Council resolution for a ceasefire in March 2024.

Speaking in July ahead of his appointment as prime minister, Andy Burnham apologised for Labour's initial response to Israel's military action in Gaza, saying the party "didn't get it right".

But, when responding at Prime Minister's Questions on 21 October, he said the proscription of Palestine Action by the previous Labour government "followed a rigorous and evidence-based process that came before this house, endorsed by Parliament".

In a statement, the Home Office said: "The Court of Appeal found that Palestine Action carried out acts of terrorism, celebrated those who took part in them and promoted the use of violence."

"Support for the organisation and financial support to benefit it is against the law."

It added: "The proscription of Palestine Action does not affect lawful protest in support of the Palestinian cause, which remains a fundamental democratic right."

articles.title: Outcry prompts ‘Call of Duty’ to cut Seoul tragedy footage
articles.summary: American video game publisher Activision said Friday that it was removing controversial footage from its newly released “Call of Duty” game after an outcry in South Korea over the inclusion of real-life footage from a deadly 2022 Halloween crowd crush in Seoul.
articles.body: American video game publisher Activision said Friday that it was removing controversial footage from its newly released “Call of Duty” game after an outcry in South Korea over the inclusion of real-life footage from a deadly 2022 Halloween crowd crush in Seoul. Last week’s global release of “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” came days before the Oct. 29 anniversary of the disaster in the South Korean capital’s nightlife district of Itaewon, where a crowd of tens of thousands of partygoers surged beyond control in a narrow alley, causing nearly 160 deaths. The game, which takes place amid a fictional North Korean invasion of the South, features about 10 seconds of heavily edited footage of the tragedy to illustrate what the aftermath of a Pyongyang attack might look like, though it does not refer to the Itaewon crowd crush directly. Groups representing families of the crowd crush victims had demanded that the footage be removed, saying it was appalling that the game had directly reproduced actual scenes of people performing CPR “while victims lay on the cold streets amid chaos and desperation.” “If the game developer has even the slightest sense of respect and empathy for the victims of the Itaewon disaster, it should promptly take corrective action,” the Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association and Itaewon Disaster Citizens’ Countermeasures Committee said in a joint statement Friday. The California-based game publisher, Activision, apologized in a statement and said the footage would be completely removed through a game update scheduled for release Nov. 12. “This game is a fictional work created to provide a realistic and immersive experience,” the company said, according to the South Korean public broadcaster MBC. “In using actual news footage in the game, we never intended to evoke any tragic incident, including the Itaewon disaster, or to trivialize the suffering associated with such tragedies.” The controversy came as grieving families are still waiting for answers about authorities’ failure to prevent the disaster four years ago. Nearly two dozen officials have been charged in the investigation, which is still underway, while three former police officers have been jailed. On Thursday, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung vowed that his government would “uncover the truth.” “On that day, when what should have been a joyful autumn night turned into the scene of a horrific tragedy, the state was nowhere to be found,” he said in a statement on X. Lee Jin Woo, whose younger sister was 28 when she died in the crowd crush, told NBC News that he had played the new “Call of Duty” game and didn’t notice the Itaewon footage at first. “But after hearing about it and thinking it over, I began to realize the footage looked very similar,” said Lee, who works at a South Korean gaming company. “The more I thought about it, the more I felt betrayed as a gamer,” he said. “After all, it was a game company and a game series that I had liked.” The game’s premise, in which South Korean conscripts are thrust into defending their country alongside American soldiers after a North Korean invasion, has been controversial since before it was available to play. Though the “Call of Duty” invasion is fictional, it draws on North Korea’s real-life capture of Seoul in 1950 during the Korean War. The conflict ended in 1953 with an armistice instead of a peace treaty, and the two Koreas remain technically at war. Tensions between the North and South have escalated in recent weeks, with the two countries embroiled in a standoff along their heavily militarized border. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has rebuffed diplomatic outreach from Washington and Seoul as he continues to advance his nuclear and ballistic missile programs. “Ultimately, whether we’re talking about an actual war or the Itaewon disaster, both involve the suffering of real people,” Lee Mi Hyun, a director at the Itaewon Disaster Citizens’ Countermeasures Committee, told NBC News in an interview. “They’re turning that suffering into entertainment,” she said. “It’s an approach that seems to show absolutely no empathy for the people who experienced that suffering.” Some South Korean lawmakers say the game should be taken as a warning. “We need to pay attention to the question it raises,” Han Dong-hoon, an opposition legislator, said last week in a Facebook post. “If that day were to come again, would we be ‘prepared’?” The game has also been defended by members of Lee’s governing Democratic Party such as Kim Han Kyu, who said there was “nothing wrong with playing a game set against the backdrop of North Korea’s nuclear weapons.” “We are still technically under an armistice, aren’t we?” he said Thursday in a Facebook post. “Wouldn’t it be even stranger if no games depicted a war against North Korea?” Others have used the game to criticize Lee’s conciliatory approach to North Korea, with opposition lawmaker Ahn Cheol Soo suggesting last week that the South Korean president try playing the game to correct his “naïve judgment” about the North Korean threat. With its “Call of Duty” franchise struggling to sustain interest in recent years, the Microsoft-owned Activision used “Modern Warfare 4” to deliver what fans loved about its previous games: a hyperrealistic military shooter. “I don’t think we were happy with every aspect of last year’s game, and we heard the feedback loud and clear,” Activision Chief Marketing Officer Tyler Bahl told “The Game Business Show” earlier this month. “With ‘Modern Warfare 4,’ we’ve tried to adjust based on that feedback. It’s getting back to a grounded military shooter. Making it cinematic, making it authentic and bringing that edge back that ‘Call of Duty’ is known for,” he said. That approach appears to have worked. As of Friday, “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” was the top-selling game in both South Korea and the United States on Steam, an online PC game distribution platform. In its review, gaming website IGN said it was a “much-needed reminder of what ‘Call of Duty’ can be at its best, even if it can’t fully recapture the heights of its glory days.”

articles.title: Miraculous escape: 100-yr-old woman falls into 50-foot well after feeling dizzy in Neemuch, survives & rescued on a cot
articles.summary: 100-year-old Jamni Bai survives 50-foot fall into open well in Neemuch; farmers rescue her on a cot and rush her to hospital with minor injuries.
articles.body: Indore: In what seems to be a miraculous escape for an elderly, a 100-year-old woman allegedly survived a 50-foot fall into an open well at a farm in Neemuch on Thursday. She had enough luck; the surface of the well was soft and filled with some water and a quick rescue by farmers saved the woman’s life.She was rescued on a cot by and later taken to the hospital on a motorcycle by her kin.The woman, identified as Jamni Bai, who has a grandson in his 40s, was sitting on the boundary of the well in Jamuniya Kalan village when she reportedly felt dizzy and fell inside.The woman’s daughter-in-law, who was working in a nearby field, was the first one to hear her cries for help from inside the well. She immediately alerted farmers working nearby and family members, who rushed to the spot. As tractors continued to operate in the surrounding fields, two men climbed down into the well, placed the elderly woman on a cot, and helped pull her out. She was then rushed to a nearby hospital on a motorcycle, where doctors said she had escaped serious injuries and was out of danger.Sarpanch Vinod Jaiswal said that the woman had a miraculous escape. “It’s even more surprising because she is a 100-year-old. articles.title: Over 95% of voters issued SIR notices in Maharashtra cleared after scrutiny
articles.summary: Maharashtra electoral roll SIR: 95%+ of 1.22 crore voters issued notices cleared; 96.51% discrepancy cases and 93.73% unmapped verified, BLAs to follow up.
articles.body: Pune: Over 95% of the 1.22 crore voters issued notices during the SIR of Maharashtra’s electoral roll have been cleared after verification of documents, according to state chief electoral officer’s office data on Oct 30.Chief electoral officer S Chockalingam said all 1.22 crore notices were served. He said voters submitting the required supporting documents would not face any problems.The district-wise report shows that 96.51% of the 62.48 lakh voters flagged for logical discrepancies in their electoral records cleared the scrutiny. On the other hand, 93.73% of the 59.75 lakh unmapped voters cleared the verification process.Chockalingam said, “Lists of remaining cases have been put up on the chief electoral officer’s website. Booth-level agents (BLAs) of political parties can check these lists and help the voters concerned submit their supporting documents.”Booth-level officers (BLOs) reached out to voters who were issued notices and ensured collection of documents in most cases. “The collection should be completed by today (Friday) in a few remaining districts,” said an electoral official.The chief electoral officer’s office has uploaded district-wise and constituency-wise lists of electors with notices pending for disposal. BLAs have been directed to contact these voters in their respective polling areas and facilitate submission of the required documents to booth-level officers (BLOs).Officials said the pending list includes only cases where verification or disposal is yet to be completed, and not all 1.22 crore voters served notices. The involvement of BLAs is expected to help the electoral machinery reach voters who have not submitted their documents.The responsibility for examining documents and deciding on individual cases rests with electoral registration officers (EROs) or assistant electoral registration officers (AEROs).Officials iterated that receiving an SIR notice did not mean that an elector’s name would be automatically deleted from the electoral roll. articles.title: Texas grand jury indicts ICE officer accused of running over man in Houston
articles.summary: The officer faces charges after allegedly striking a fleeing construction worker with an SUV during an immigration raid.
articles.body:
A grand jury in Texas has indicted a United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer accused of deliberately running over a Mexican construction worker during an operation in Houston this month.

ICE officer Mario Alberto Morales faces charges of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon for the October 10 incident, Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare announced on Friday.

Criminal charges against federal immigration officers have been rare during President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, although several encounters involving officers have prompted investigations.

Morales is accused of striking 48-year-old Miguel Parra-Hernandez, an immigrant who has lived in Harris County for more than 30 years. Teare said that Parra-Hernandez had no criminal record.

Parra-Hernandez was running away from federal agents when an unmarked black Jeep Cherokee struck him in a car park near Clay Road and Highway 6, according to investigators. He suffered multiple fractures to his right leg and an ankle injury which required surgery.

The indictment follows a dispute between local prosecutors and federal authorities over what happened. ICE has maintained that Parra-Hernandez ran in front of the vehicle, dismissing the allegations that the officer intentionally struck him as “reckless and false.”

But Teare has said surveillance video contradicts the agency’s account.

It shows the SUV crossing a median and pursuing Parra-Hernandez as he runs away. Although another vehicle obscures the moment of impact, the video shows the man on the ground moments later.

Authorities also released body-camera footage on Friday. In the recording, Morales can be heard acknowledging that he struck Parra-Hernandez with his vehicle.

Teare also accused federal authorities of failing to cooperate with the investigation, including by removing the Jeep before local investigators could examine it for potential evidence.

A search warrant obtained by local media shows investigators had not been granted access to the vehicle as of October 23.

The case has also raised questions about the operation’s intended target. ICE said agents were searching for a man identified as Jose Mendoza-Cervantes, whom they believed to be travelling with Parra-Hernandez.

But Mendoza-Cervantes’s daughter told The New York Times that her father died in 2017. Parra-Hernandez’s family has disputed that the two men knew each other.

The Morales indictment comes as the Harris County District Attorney’s Office continues investigating the fatal shooting of another Mexican, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo , on July 7.

An ICE officer, Gregory Feathers, has been accused of firing at the vehicle Salgado Araujo was driving on his way to work in Houston.

Federal authorities said the officer acted in self-defence, a claim the surviving passengers in the vehicle dispute.
